description: Authored exact-caption fallback lines. No voice audio is bundled or claimed generated. NONE means silence. HEARD_RHYTHM requires accepted sustained elevation AND near creature; it is fiction, not a fear/health diagnosis.

lines.text: Containment failure. Field team, proceed to the emergency observation shelter.
The shelter is sealed. You have a terminal, three remote emitters, one emergency isolation switch, and a locked basement door.
Silence the faults. Each stage releases one basement lock. Four locks, then you get out.
The sedative is wearing off. Working makes noise. Staying here does not finish the protocol.
Click the computer in the room, or press E, to use its controls.
Listen: each machine plays its own sound in turn. Then press the number of the machine making the noise. Wrong ones clang.

Press Q, the orange QUIET button on your remote, or turn around and pull the lever down, to silence the machines. Silent machines lower exposure. A real run has three cells. Act when its footsteps get loud; at the wall it is too late.
Listen for receding footsteps. Captions carry the same clue.

Hold F, the green button on your remote, or push the lever up and hold it, for one second to bring the power back. In a real run you choose when: wait until the footsteps fade. It ends by itself after 25 seconds. Your work is saved.
Press R to watch four pulses. Replay is always free.
Repeat the practice sequence. Real sequences are longer.
Press T to send the heartbeat away from the shelter.
This is a recorded message from Doctor Elias Hale, director of this station. If you are hearing it, the shelter has sealed itself around you, and the specimen is loose.
Listen carefully. It is nearly blind, but it hears everything. Every machine you run, every mistake you make. Give it enough noise, and it will come through that door.
There is one way out: the basement. Its door has four locks, and each research protocol on the terminal in front of you releases one.

When its footsteps come close, press Q, or pull the lever behind you, and the machines go silent. Wait until the steps fade, then hold F to bring the power back. You have three cells. Spend them carefully.
The emitters outside can play a heartbeat from somewhere else, and it will hunt the sound. So keep your own heart steady. It can hear that too.
I have patched a line through to someone on the outside. They have the manuals you do not. Tell them what you hear and see, and they will tell you what to press.
You have five minutes before the sedative wears off completely. After that, nothing in here will hold it. Four locks. Then you run. Good luck.

First protocol: six rack faults, a cable patch and a broken conduit, in whatever order the terminal gives them. For the faults, listen as each machine plays its sound, then press the number of the one that sounds wrong.
First protocol: six rack faults, a cable patch and a broken conduit, in the order the terminal gives them. Describe what you hear and see to your friend, and they will tell you what to press.
Machines quiet. It may still investigate the last sound. Prepare emitter A.
First lock released. Second protocol: repeat the signal sequence and copy the heartbeat on the screen, then send it out through emitter A.
It took the bait. Second lock released. Third protocol: the rack is overloading, eight faults, two at a time. There are twelve cables to patch, and you will have to find it on the radar.
Thirty-six faults across the rack. Up to three fail together. Work one at a time.
Overload cleared. Third lock released. Emitter B will draw it further from the door.
Third lock released. Last protocol: a longer sequence, and slow, steady breathing until it loses your trail. Then send it out through emitter B.
Fourth lock released. One last decoy, then the basement door.
Fourth lock released. Press T to send the last decoy. The door motor starts once it holds, and it is loud.
Decoy broadcast active. Basement lock cycle running.
Basement door opening. Go.
Main power lost. Emergency isolation remains available.
Breach attempt. Press Q to isolate equipment now.
Footsteps receding. Hold F to restore equipment.
Pulse signal unavailable. Gameplay is using neutral settings.
Baseline recorded. Pulse input is active.
I heard that. Do it again.
You made it quiet. I know you are still in there.
A rhythm behind the wall.
Over there.
The marked boxes are faults. Q buys quiet time; it will not finish the work.
There is no penalty for replay. Press R, repeat four inputs, then T.
Shelter integrity lost.
I can hear you working.
